answer: Continuous work ledger. Each identity must submit a fresh pulse of solved compute tied to its prior session state, and validators only advance entries whose history chains without gaps. An attacker can forge a single entry cheaply, but sustaining many identities requires real machine-hours and distinct hardware fingerprints logged as an onyx marker in each block. Duplicating one identity across N slots thus costs N times the sustained compute plus continuous uptime, not a one-time payment.
